reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on very easy, consistent runs, it lacks any structured aerobic development or stimulus. Plan B incorporates cross-training and longer, conversational-paced runs, which are crucial for building the aerobic base necessary for faster trail running. The inclusion of cross-training also helps with recovery and injury prevention, something Plan A neglects. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs could lead to plateaus, whereas Plan B’s varied approach will likely promote greater progress.
